certificates.title: AI Literacy
certificates.description: The course covered what AI is, how it learns and improves, how it differs from automation, and the forms and enabling technologies behind AI applications. I explored its benefits and everyday and industry applications, identified data challenges it can help solve, and practiced using an AI assistant to improve a solution and create a product launch plan.
certificates.imageAlt: IBM SkillsBuild AI Literacy certificate issued to Erica Santini de Lima

details: As part of the Aquiweb development team, built and deployed full-stack features for client organizations whose MES systems served 100+ users, including managers and shop-floor operators, supporting production, inventory, and equipment workflows.
Built REST API integrations and data import/export workflows.

Built a CSV import workflow that processed 20,000+ complex operations across multiple work orders, some with hundreds of operations. Added validation, post-import processing, and dependency creation, with transactional rollback to prevent partial imports.
Implemented backend stock checks that prevented users from recording material consumption above available inventory.
Created client-specific operational reports using JasperReports.
Investigated production issues using logs, SQL queries, and workflow reproduction; traced causes, tested fixes, and supported releases.

Collaborated with developers, functional consultants, and clients to clarify requirements and document technical work; participated in testing, code reviews, sprint planning, and GitLab/Jenkins CI/CD workflows.
Used OpenAI Codex for codebase exploration, debugging, test support, and documentation, reviewing suggestions against the code and requirements.
Customized and maintained Sage X3 ERP functionality using Sage X3 4GL and SQL, primarily in a client-consulting context.
Adapted existing ERP behavior and functionality to client requirements and workflows.
Investigated application and database issues, reproduced defects, tested changes, and supported technical troubleshooting.
Worked directly with English- and French-speaking clients to clarify requirements and validate solutions.
Created and maintained client-specific Crystal Reports, including formulas, conditional logic, parameters, formatting, and subreports.

Streamlined the internal weekly pizza-ordering process for 40+ employees by proposing and implementing an automated workflow with a shared spreadsheet and Power Automate. It replaced manual order collection, tallied pizza choices and dietary requests, sent a reminder the day before, and reset weekly; it remains in use after more than 3 years.
Built a Node.js prototype integrated with the Sage X3 REST API to retrieve manufacturing order data and display it in a web interface with a weekly calendar.
Developed and debugged mobile game functionality using C# and Unity.
Participated in Agile development, sprint planning, estimation using Planning Poker, testing, QA, bug tracking and documentation, and release delivery.
Supported feature implementation and validated functionality before releases.
Served as acting Scrum Master for a small mobile game development team.
Supported sprint planning, task organization, team coordination, communication, problem solving, and delivery, including estimation using Planning Poker.

details: Graduated at the top of the class with a 94% weighted average.
Coursework covered web development, JavaScript, Node.js, databases, object-oriented programming, and other areas of the program.
Invited by my programming professor to tutor classmates in C++ for one semester.
Completed hands-on Arduino coursework and built small personal Arduino projects.
Received a research scholarship for two consecutive semesters.
Participated in a Junior Enterprise focused on business consulting and strategic planning.
Completed a student exchange at Université du Québec à Montréal (UQAM).
Completed coursework in data structures, algorithms, C, C++, object-oriented programming, and databases.
Tutored fellow students in C programming for two semesters.
Competed in an ICPC programming contest after my Logic and Algorithms professor selected me as one of two students.
Helped deliver introductory logic-programming workshops for high school students.
